searchText: Idea for running two EL nodes: 1. EL1 is connected to the network, downloads new blocks and sometimes produces one for a CL validator. 2. EL2 is offline. 3. When EL1 gets a new valid block it also pushes it to EL2 (via import) and checks if EL2 confirms it is valid. 4. For blocks produced by EL1 it also pushes it to EL2 for validation. 5. In case of any disagreement between EL1 and EL2 the CL validator stops attesting. Why not just have the CL push new payloads to multiple ELs? Does it mean both ELs need p2p network access? There are some cases when EL1 would be syncing using an EL network, if EL2 doesn't support the same sync strategy as EL1 it would be difficult to keep them both in sync unless EL2 is also connected to the network The goal is to stop attestation in case of bug instead of attesting to a buggy output.

Idea for running two EL nodes:
1. EL1 is connected to the network, downloads new blocks and sometimes produces one for a CL validator.
2. EL2 is offline.
3. When EL1 gets a new valid block it also pushes it to EL2 (via import) and checks if EL2 confirms it is valid.
4. For blocks produced by EL1 it also pushes it to EL2 for validation.
5. In case of any disagreement between EL1 and EL2 the CL validator stops attesting.
